questions.question_text: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?

options.A: The Chief Justice of India
options.B: The Vice-President of India
options.C: The Prime Minister
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Under Article 60, the President takes the oath before the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most available judge of the Supreme Court.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The Vice-President takes his own oath before the President. | Trap (C): The Prime Minister is sworn in by the President, not the other way round. | Trap (D): The Speaker has no role in the President's oath.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha?

options.A: 21 years
options.B: 25 years
options.C: 30 years
options.D: 35 years

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 84(b): a member of the House of the People must be at least 25 years old.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): 21 is the minimum age for panchayat and municipal elections, not the Lok Sabha. | Trap (C): 30 is the minimum age for the Rajya Sabha. | Trap (D): 35 is the minimum age for the President and Vice-President.

questions.question_text: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?

options.A: Part II
options.B: Part III
options.C: Part IV-A
options.D: Part IV

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Part III (Articles 12–35) contains the Fundamental Rights.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Part II deals with citizenship. | Trap (C): Part IV-A contains the Fundamental Duties. | Trap (D): Part IV contains the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question_text: Who appoints the Governor of a State in India?

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.B: The Chief Justice of the High Court
options.C: The President of India
options.D: The Chief Minister of the State

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 155: the Governor of a State is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The President acts on the Union Cabinet's advice, but the appointing authority is the President. | Trap (B): The Chief Justice of the High Court administers the Governor's oath, not the appointment. | Trap (D): The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.

questions.question_text: The idea of a Concurrent List in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the constitution of which country?

options.A: Australia
options.B: Canada
options.C: Ireland
options.D: United States of America

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Concurrent List, joint sitting of the Houses, and freedom of trade and commerce were borrowed from the Australian Constitution.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Canada gave the idea of a federation with a strong Centre and residuary powers with the Centre. | Trap (C): Ireland gave the Directive Principles. | Trap (D): The USA gave Fundamental Rights and judicial review.

questions.question_text: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A of the Constitution of India today?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 10 Fundamental Duties; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th, clause (k), on education for children aged 6–14.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Overcounts; there are 11 duties in clauses (a) to (k). | Trap (B): Six is the number of categories of Fundamental Rights. | Trap (D): 10 were added in 1976; the 11th came in 2002.

questions.question_text: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 80(1)(a) and (3): the President nominates 12 members with special knowledge of literature, science, art and social service.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Undercounts: Article 80 allows 12 nominees. | Trap (C): Overcounts: Article 80 allows 12 nominees. | Trap (D): Two Anglo-Indian members could earlier be nominated to the Lok Sabha; that provision ended in 2020.
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: Anglo-Indian trap refers to the 104th Amendment, 2020.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the election of the Vice-President of India is correct?

options.A: He is elected by the Lok Sabha alone, by a simple majority of members present and voting.
options.B: He is elected by all members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members; State Assemblies take no part.
options.C: He is elected by the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies.
options.D: He is elected by the elected members of both Houses only; nominated members cannot vote.

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 66(1): the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of the members of both Houses of Parliament, by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. Nominated members are included; State Legislatures are not.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Both Houses form the electoral college. | Trap (C): That describes the President's electoral college. | Trap (D): Nominated members do vote in the Vice-Presidential election (unlike the Presidential one).

questions.question_text: Who was popularly known as 'Frontier Gandhi'?

questions.question_text: The ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, the Arthashastra, is attributed to:

options.A: Kalidasa
options.B: Kautilya (Chanakya)
options.C: Banabhatta

questions.question_text: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out under which Viceroy?

options.A: Lord Hardinge
options.B: Lord Minto
options.C: Lord Ripon
options.D: Lord Curzon

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal, effective 16 October 1905. It provoked the Swadeshi movement and was annulled in 1911.

questions.question_text: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between the Mughal forces of Akbar and:

options.A: Maharana Pratap of Mewar
options.B: Rana Sanga
options.C: Hemu
options.D: Shivaji

questions.question_text: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by:

questions.question_text: At which session did the Indian National Congress adopt the 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) resolution in December 1929?

questions.pedagogical_explanation: At the Lahore session (December 1929), under Nehru, Congress declared Purna Swaraj its goal; 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The 1916 Lucknow session is known for the Congress–League pact. | Trap (C): The 1938 Haripura session was Bose's first presidency. | Trap (D): The 1931 Karachi session adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following events in chronological order: (1) Arrival of the Simon Commission, (2) Gandhi–Irwin Pact, (3) Launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement, (4) Cripps Mission.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Non-Cooperation: 1920. Simon Commission arrived: February 1928. Gandhi–Irwin Pact: March 1931. Cripps Mission: March 1942.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Places the Cripps Mission (1942) before the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931). | Trap (B): Places the Simon Commission (1928) before Non-Cooperation (1920). | Trap (C): Places the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931) before the Simon Commission (1928).

questions.question_text: Which Indian state is known as the 'Land of Five Rivers'?

questions.question_text: Which is generally regarded as the largest freshwater lake in India?

options.A: Dal Lake
options.B: Sambhar Lake

questions.question_text: What is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh?

options.A: Aizawl
options.B: Dispur

options.D: Kohima

questions.question_text: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent floods and shifting course?

options.A: Gandak
options.B: Son
options.C: Kosi
options.D: Damodar

questions.question_text: Black soil, also called regur, is best suited for growing which crop?

questions.question_text: Which strait separates Asia from North America?

questions.question_text:
Match the national parks with the states in which they are located.

(P) Kaziranga (Q) Gir (R) Periyar (S) Jim Corbett

questions.question_text: Which of the following arranges these mountain ranges correctly from north to south?

questions.question_text: Inflation refers to:

options.A: a rise in the price of one commodity
options.B: an increase in a country's exports
options.C: a sustained rise in the general price level
options.D: a rise in the value of money

questions.question_text: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Union Budget laid before Parliament as the 'Annual Financial Statement'?

options.A: Article 112
options.B: Article 202
options.C: Article 110
options.D: Article 114

questions.question_text: In the Indian context, 'disinvestment' means:

options.A: closing down loss-making factories
options.B: the government selling part of its equity in public sector enterprises
options.C: the government buying shares in private companies
options.D: foreign investors withdrawing money from Indian markets

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Disinvestment is the sale or liquidation of the government's stake in public sector undertakings.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Closure is different from selling equity. | Trap (C): That is investment, the opposite. | Trap (D): That is capital outflow, not disinvestment.

questions.question_text: GDP at factor cost is obtained from GDP at market prices by subtracting:

options.A: net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies)
options.B: net factor income from abroad
options.C: depreciation (consumption of fixed capital)
options.D: direct taxes such as income tax

questions.pedagogical_explanation: GDP at market prices includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies. GDPfc = GDPmp − indirect taxes + subsidies = GDPmp − net indirect taxes.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Adding net factor income from abroad turns GDP into GNP; it is not the market-price-to-factor-cost step. | Trap (C): Subtracting depreciation gives net domestic product, not factor cost. | Trap (D): Direct taxes are paid out of factor incomes, so they are not removed.

questions.question_text: What is the chemical formula of common salt?

options.A: KCl
options.B: NaCl
options.C: CaCO3
options.D: NaHCO3

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Potassium chloride, a different salt. | Trap (C): Calcium carbonate, limestone or chalk. | Trap (D): Sodium bicarbonate, baking soda.

questions.question_text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?

options.A: Jupiter
options.B: Venus
options.C: Mercury
options.D: Mars

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Iron oxide (rust) in the soil gives Mars its reddish colour.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Jupiter is the largest planet, known for its Great Red Spot. | Trap (B): Venus is the brightest planet and is called the Morning or Evening Star. | Trap (C): Mercury is the smallest planet, closest to the Sun.

questions.question_text: What is the SI unit of force?

options.A: Joule
options.B: Watt
options.C: Pascal
options.D: Newton

questions.pedagogical_explanation: One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The joule is the unit of work and energy. | Trap (B): The watt is the unit of power. | Trap (C): The pascal is the unit of pressure.

questions.question_text: Deficiency of iodine in the diet commonly causes:

options.A: anaemia
options.B: night blindness
options.C: rickets
options.D: goitre

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormones; its lack causes the thyroid to enlarge (goitre).
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Anaemia commonly results from iron deficiency. | Trap (B): Night blindness results from vitamin A deficiency. | Trap (C): Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency.

questions.question_text: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Pure water is neutral; at 25 °C its hydrogen-ion concentration is 10⁻⁷ mol/L, so pH = 7.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): pH 0 is strongly acidic. | Trap (B): pH 14 is strongly basic. | Trap (D): pH 1 is strongly acidic.

questions.question_text: Sound cannot travel through:

options.A: air
options.B: water
options.C: a vacuum
options.D: steel

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium; it cannot travel through empty space.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Air is the usual medium for sound. | Trap (B): Sound travels faster in water than in air. | Trap (D): Sound travels fastest in solids such as steel.

questions.question_text: Which blood cells play the main role in blood clotting?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Neutrophils
options.C: Lymphocytes
options.D: Red blood cells

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) release factors that start clotting and form a plug at the wound.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Neutrophils are white cells that engulf microbes. | Trap (C): Lymphocytes are white cells involved in immunity. | Trap (D): RBCs carry oxygen using haemoglobin.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of atomic number: carbon, oxygen, sodium, helium.

options.A: Carbon, helium, oxygen, sodium
options.B: Helium, carbon, sodium, oxygen
options.C: Helium, carbon, oxygen, sodium
options.D: Helium, oxygen, carbon, sodium

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Atomic numbers: helium 2, carbon 6, oxygen 8, sodium 11.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Puts carbon (6) before helium (2). | Trap (B): Puts sodium (11) before oxygen (8). | Trap (D): Puts oxygen (8) before carbon (6).

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Gitanjali'?

options.A: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
options.B: Sarojini Naidu
options.C: Rabindranath Tagore
options.D: Premchand

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Tagore's 'Gitanjali' (English version 1912) led to his Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): He wrote 'Anandamath', which contains 'Vande Mataram'. | Trap (B): She wrote 'The Golden Threshold'. | Trap (D): He wrote 'Godaan' and many Hindi–Urdu stories.
questions.concept_tag: GK – Static – International organisations, awards and books

questions.question_text: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?

options.A: Geneva
options.B: New York
options.C: Vienna
options.D: Paris

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York City; the General Assembly and Security Council meet there.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Geneva hosts the UN's European office and many agencies. | Trap (C): Vienna hosts another UN office and the IAEA. | Trap (D): Paris hosts UNESCO.
questions.concept_tag: GK – Static – International organisations, awards and books

questions.question_text: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in the field of:

options.A: journalism
options.B: cinema
options.C: sports
options.D: literature

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Named after Dadasaheb Phalke, maker of 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913), it honours lifetime contribution to Indian cinema.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): No such journalism link; the award is for film. | Trap (C): The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is the top sports award. | Trap (D): The Jnanpith Award is the top literary award.
questions.concept_tag: GK – Static – International organisations, awards and books

questions.question_text: Where is the secretariat of SAARC located?

options.A: Kathmandu
options.B: Dhaka
options.C: New Delhi
options.D: Colombo

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (founded 1985) has its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Dhaka hosts the BIMSTEC secretariat. | Trap (C): India is a member, but the secretariat is not in Delhi. | Trap (D): Colombo hosts the Colombo Plan secretariat.
questions.concept_tag: GK – Static – International organisations, awards and books

questions.question_text: 'Wings of Fire', an autobiography, was written by:

options.A: Vikram Sarabhai
options.B: Satish Dhawan
options.C: Homi J. Bhabha
options.D: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (with Arun Tiwari)

questions.pedagogical_explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) is Dr. Kalam's autobiography, written with Arun Tiwari.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Sarabhai founded India's space programme but did not write this book. | Trap (B): Dhawan headed ISRO; he did not write this book. | Trap (C): Bhabha led India's nuclear programme; he did not write this book.
questions.concept_tag: GK – Static – International organisations, awards and books

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the G20 is correct?

options.A: The G20 was founded in 2008 as a summit of heads of state and government.
options.B: India has never held the G20 presidency.
options.C: The G20 has a permanent secretariat in Geneva.
options.D: The African Union became a permanent member at the New Delhi Summit in 2023.

questions.pedagogical_explanation: At the New Delhi Leaders' Summit (9–10 September 2023), under India's presidency, the African Union was admitted as a permanent member.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The G20 began in 1999 as a forum of finance ministers and central bank governors; leaders' summits began in 2008. | Trap (B): India held the presidency in 2023 and hosted the New Delhi Summit. | Trap (C): The G20 has no permanent secretariat; the presidency rotates.
questions.concept_tag: GK – Static – International organisations, awards and books
questions.review_note: Time-sensitive: Web-checked 12 Nov 2026: AU admitted as permanent member 9 Sep 2023 at New Delhi; G20 founded 1999 as a finance ministers/central bank governors forum, first leaders summit 2008; no permanent secretariat. All four options hold. Stable.

questions.question_text: Pope Leo XIV, elected in May 2025, is the first pope from which country?

options.A: Italy
options.B: Argentina
options.C: United States of America
options.D: Peru

questions.pedagogical_explanation: On 8 May 2025, the conclave elected Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost, born in Chicago, who took the name Leo XIV (Vatican News; AP).
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Many earlier popes were Italian, but Leo XIV was born in Chicago. | Trap (B): His predecessor, Pope Francis, was from Argentina. | Trap (D): He served for many years in Peru and holds Peruvian citizenship, but he was born in the USA.
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: Peru trap is deliberate (Peruvian citizen, born in the USA). | Time-sensitive: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Prevost), elected 8 May 2025; first US-born pope. Office-holder fact: valid while he is pope.

questions.question_text: India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 by beating which team in the final at Ahmedabad?

options.A: New Zealand
options.B: Australia
options.C: South Africa
options.D: England

questions.pedagogical_explanation: On 8 March 2026 at Ahmedabad, India beat New Zealand by 96 runs to defend the title they won in 2024 (ICC; BBC Sport).
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Australia did not play the 2026 final. | Trap (C): India beat South Africa in the 2024 final at Barbados. | Trap (D): England did not play the 2026 final.
questions.review_note: Time-sensitive: Men's T20 World Cup 2026 final, 8 Mar 2026, Ahmedabad: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs. Past event; stable. Stem says '2026', so it stays correct after the next edition.

questions.question_text: Operation Sindoor, launched by India on 7 May 2025, was a response to:

options.A: the Pulwama attack on a CRPF convoy in February 2019
options.B: the terrorist attack at Pahalgam on 22 April 2025
options.C: the Uri attack on an Army base in September 2016
options.D: the Mumbai attacks of November 2008

questions.pedagogical_explanation: On 7 May 2025, Indian forces struck nine terrorist sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir in response to the 22 April Pahalgam attack (PIB; MEA briefing, 7 May 2025).
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Pulwama led to the Balakot air strike in 2019. | Trap (C): Uri led to the 2016 surgical strikes. | Trap (D): 26/11 was in 2008; Operation Sindoor came much later.
questions.review_note: Time-sensitive: Operation Sindoor, 7 May 2025, after the Pahalgam attack of 22 Apr 2025. Past event; stable. Wording kept to the official PIB/MEA description (nine terrorist sites).

questions.question_text: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 was awarded to Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for developing:

options.A: click chemistry
options.B: lithium-ion batteries
options.C: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing
options.D: metal–organic frameworks (MOFs)

questions.pedagogical_explanation: MOFs are porous crystals of metal ions linked by organic molecules, used for capturing gases, harvesting water and storing chemicals (nobelprize.org, 2025).
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): That won the Chemistry Prize in 2022. | Trap (B): That won the Chemistry Prize in 2019. | Trap (C): That won the Chemistry Prize in 2020.
questions.review_note: Time-sensitive: Nobel Chemistry 2025 (MOFs). Stable.

questions.question_text: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025 (Brunkow, Ramsdell and Sakaguchi) recognised discoveries about:

options.A: microRNA and gene regulation
options.B: mRNA vaccines against COVID-19
options.C: circadian rhythms
options.D: peripheral immune tolerance

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The 2025 laureates were honoured 'for their discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance', which identified regulatory T cells that stop the immune system attacking the body (nobelprize.org, 2025).
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): That won the Medicine Prize in 2024. | Trap (B): That won the Medicine Prize in 2023. | Trap (C): That won the Medicine Prize in 2017.
questions.review_note: Time-sensitive: Nobel Medicine 2025 (peripheral immune tolerance). Stable.

questions.question_text:
Match the 2025 Nobel Prizes with the work they recognised.

(P) Physics (Q) Chemistry (R) Physiology or Medicine (S) Economic Sciences

(1) innovation-driven economic growth (2) peripheral immune tolerance (3) macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit (4) metal–organic frameworks
questions.pedagogical_explanation: 2025: Physics – Clarke, Devoret, Martinis (macroscopic quantum tunnelling); Chemistry – Kitagawa, Robson, Yaghi (MOFs); Medicine – Brunkow, Ramsdell, Sakaguchi (peripheral immune tolerance); Economics – Mokyr, Aghion, Howitt (innovation-driven growth) (nobelprize.org).
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Swaps Chemistry and Medicine. | Trap (C): Swaps Medicine and Economics. | Trap (D): Swaps Physics and Chemistry.
questions.review_note: Time-sensitive: All four 2025 Nobel science/economics prizes. Stable.

questions.question_text: Who is the first law officer of the Government of India?

options.A: The Solicitor General of India
options.B: The Union Law Minister
options.C: The Attorney General of India
options.D: The Chief Justice of India

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 76: the Attorney General is the highest law officer and gives legal advice to the Government of India.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General. | Trap (B): The Law Minister is a political executive, not the law officer. | Trap (D): The CJI heads the judiciary; he is not the government's law officer.

questions.question_text: Disputes relating to the election of the President of India are decided by:

options.A: the Supreme Court of India
options.B: the Vice-President of India
options.C: the Parliament of India
options.D: the Election Commission of India

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 71: all doubts and disputes arising out of the election of a President or Vice-President are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The Vice-President has no such role. | Trap (C): Parliament has no power to decide such disputes. | Trap (D): The EC conducts the election but does not decide election disputes.

questions.question_text: What is the term of office of a member of the Rajya Sabha?

options.A: Until the House is dissolved
options.B: Six years
options.C: Four years
options.D: Five years

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Rajya Sabha members serve six years; one-third retire every second year.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is never dissolved. | Trap (C): No House has a four-year term. | Trap (D): That is the normal term of the Lok Sabha.

questions.question_text: The procedure for the impeachment of the President of India is laid down in which Article?

options.A: Article 61
options.B: Article 356
options.C: Article 72
options.D: Article 124

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 61: the President may be impeached for 'violation of the Constitution' by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Article 356 deals with President's Rule in States. | Trap (C): Article 72 deals with the President's pardoning power. | Trap (D): Article 124 deals with the Supreme Court and the removal of its judges.

questions.question_text: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 under which Article of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 280
options.B: Article 262
options.C: Article 312
options.D: Article 263

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 263 lets the President set up an Inter-State Council; it was constituted in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission. | Trap (B): Article 262 deals with inter-state river water disputes. | Trap (C): Article 312 deals with All-India Services.

questions.question_text: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, is known for:

options.A: giving constitutional status to municipalities
options.B: lowering the voting age from 21 to 18 years
options.C: adding the Tenth Schedule on anti-defection
options.D: making elementary education a Fundamental Right

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The 61st Amendment amended Article 326 to reduce the voting age to 18 years.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): That was the 74th Amendment, 1992. | Trap (C): That was the 52nd Amendment, 1985. | Trap (D): That was the 86th Amendment, 2002.

questions.question_text: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India contains provisions for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram?

options.A: Seventh Schedule
options.B: Ninth Schedule
options.C: Sixth Schedule
options.D: Fifth Schedule

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils in the tribal areas of these four north-eastern States.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Seventh Schedule contains the Union, State and Concurrent Lists. | Trap (B): The Ninth Schedule lists laws protected from certain challenges. | Trap (D): The Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas in other States.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha.
2. The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses.
3. The Speaker submits the resignation letter to the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.A: 1, 2 and 3
options.B: 2 and 3 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only
options.D: 1 and 2 only

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 94(c) allows removal by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members (after 14 days' notice); Article 118(4) makes the Speaker preside over a joint sitting; under Article 94 the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Statement 3 is wrong: the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker. | Trap (B): Statement 3 is wrong, and statement 1 is correct. | Trap (C): Statement 3 is wrong, and statement 2 is correct.

questions.question_text: Who founded the Sur dynasty and introduced the silver coin called the 'rupiya'?

options.A: Alauddin Khalji
options.B: Sher Shah Suri
options.C: Humayun
options.D: Akbar

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Sher Shah Suri (r. 1540–45) founded the Sur dynasty and issued the silver rupiya.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Khalji is known for market reforms, not the rupiya. | Trap (C): Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah. | Trap (D): Akbar was a Mughal emperor; the rupiya predates his reign.

questions.question_text: The ancient university of Nalanda was located in present-day:

options.A: Uttar Pradesh
options.B: Odisha
options.C: Gujarat
options.D: Bihar

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Nalanda, a great Buddhist monastic university, lies near Rajgir in Bihar.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Sarnath, not Nalanda, is in Uttar Pradesh. | Trap (B): Odisha had Pushpagiri, not Nalanda. | Trap (C): Gujarat had Valabhi, another ancient centre of learning.

questions.question_text: The Khilafat Movement (1919–24) was launched mainly in support of:

options.A: the King of Afghanistan
options.B: the Mughal emperor in Delhi
options.C: the Ottoman Sultan as Caliph
options.D: the Nawab of Awadh

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Indian Muslims protested against the treatment of the Ottoman Sultan, the Khalifa, after the First World War; Gandhi linked it with Non-Cooperation.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Afghanistan was not the issue. | Trap (B): The Mughal empire had ended in 1857. | Trap (D): Awadh had been annexed in 1856.

questions.question_text: The Kushana ruler Kanishka is associated with which Buddhist council?

options.A: The Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir
options.B: The Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra
options.C: The First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha
options.D: The Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Fourth Council was held under Kanishka in Kashmir (Kundalavana); it is linked with the rise of Mahayana.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Held under Ashoka. | Trap (C): Held soon after the Buddha's death under Ajatashatru. | Trap (D): Held under Kalasoka.
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: Fourth Council location given as Kashmir; some texts name Kundalavana or Jalandhar.

questions.question_text: The Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946. Who led it?

options.A: Lord Pethick-Lawrence
options.B: Lord Wavell
options.C: Sir John Simon
options.D: Sir Stafford Cripps alone

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Cabinet Mission (March 1946) comprised Pethick-Lawrence (leader), Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Wavell was the Viceroy at the time. | Trap (C): Simon led the 1928 commission. | Trap (D): Cripps was a member, but the leader was Pethick-Lawrence.

questions.question_text: The 'Permanent Settlement' of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by:

options.A: Lord Cornwallis
options.B: Lord Dalhousie
options.C: Warren Hastings
options.D: Lord Wellesley

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Cornwallis fixed the revenue permanently with the zamindars of Bengal in 1793.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Dalhousie is known for the Doctrine of Lapse. | Trap (C): Hastings preceded Cornwallis and tried short-term farming of revenue. | Trap (D): Wellesley is known for the Subsidiary Alliance.

questions.question_text: Who founded the newspaper 'Kesari'?

options.A: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
options.B: Dadabhai Naoroji
options.C: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
options.D: Lala Lajpat Rai

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Tilak started the Marathi weekly Kesari (and the English Mahratta) in 1881.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society. | Trap (B): Naoroji is known for the drain theory. | Trap (D): Lajpat Rai was associated with the Punjabi press.

questions.question_text:
Match the following leaders with the organisations they founded.

(P) Jyotiba Phule (Q) Sree Narayana Guru (R) Raja Ram Mohan Roy (S) Annie Besant
(1) Brahmo Samaj (2) Satyashodhak Samaj (3) Home Rule League (Madras) (4) SNDP Yogam
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873); Sree Narayana Guru inspired the SNDP Yogam (1903); Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828); Besant founded the Home Rule League in Madras (1916).
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Swaps Roy and Besant. | Trap (C): Swaps Phule and Roy. | Trap (D): Swaps Phule and Sree Narayana Guru.

questions.question_text: Loktak Lake, known for its floating masses of vegetation called phumdis, is in which State?

options.A: Assam
options.B: Manipur
options.C: Meghalaya
options.D: Tripura

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Loktak, in Manipur, has floating phumdis; Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park, lies on it.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Assam has Deepor Beel, not Loktak. | Trap (C): Meghalaya has Umiam Lake. | Trap (D): Tripura has Rudrasagar Lake.

questions.question_text: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon in India, is in which State?

options.A: Andhra Pradesh
options.B: Kerala
options.C: West Bengal
options.D: Odisha

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Chilika, on the Odisha coast, is India's largest coastal lagoon and a Ramsar site.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Andhra Pradesh has Kolleru and shares Pulicat. | Trap (B): Kerala has Vembanad. | Trap (C): West Bengal has no lagoon of this size.

questions.question_text: Majuli, one of the world's largest river islands, is in which river?

options.A: Mahanadi
options.B: Ganga
options.C: Godavari
options.D: Brahmaputra

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Majuli, in Assam, is a river island in the Brahmaputra and was made a district in 2016.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Majuli is in Assam, not on the Mahanadi. | Trap (B): Majuli is not on the Ganga. | Trap (C): The Godavari delta has islands, but not Majuli.

questions.question_text: Indira Point, the southernmost point of India, is located on which island?

options.A: Great Nicobar
options.B: Minicoy
options.C: Little Andaman
options.D: Car Nicobar

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Indira Point lies at the southern tip of Great Nicobar Island.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Minicoy is in Lakshadweep. | Trap (C): Little Andaman is north of the Ten Degree Channel. | Trap (D): Car Nicobar is in the northern Nicobars.

questions.question_text: Laterite soil is formed mainly as a result of:

options.A: accumulation of salts in poorly drained arid land
options.B: weathering of basalt lava in a dry climate
options.C: intense leaching in areas of high temperature and heavy rainfall
options.D: deposition of silt by rivers in flood plains

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Heavy rain leaches away silica and lime, leaving iron and aluminium oxides: laterite.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): That forms saline soil. | Trap (B): That forms black (regur) soil. | Trap (D): That forms alluvial soil.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the highest peak lying entirely within India's territory?

options.A: Mount Everest
options.B: Kamet
options.C: Nanda Devi
options.D: Kangchenjunga

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Nanda Devi (7,816 m) in Uttarakhand is the highest peak lying wholly within India; Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is higher but straddles the Sikkim–Nepal border.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Everest is on the Nepal–China border. | Trap (B): Kamet is lower than Nanda Devi. | Trap (D): Higher, but it lies on the India–Nepal border, so it is not entirely within India.

questions.question_text:
Arrange the following rivers from north to south according to where they meet the sea on India's east coast:
1. Krishna 2. Mahanadi 3. Kaveri 4. Godavari
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Mahanadi (Odisha) → Godavari (north Andhra coast) → Krishna (south Andhra coast) → Kaveri (Tamil Nadu).
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Puts the Krishna mouth north of the Godavari. | Trap (C): Puts the Godavari mouth north of the Mahanadi. | Trap (D): Puts the Kaveri mouth north of the Krishna.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Lakshadweep islands are of coral origin.
2. The Siachen Glacier lies in the Karakoram range.
3. The Western Ghats are higher on average than the Eastern Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.A: 2 and 3 only
options.B: 1, 2 and 3
options.C: 1 and 2 only
options.D: 1 and 3 only

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Lakshadweep consists of coral atolls and reefs; Siachen is in the eastern Karakoram; the Western Ghats are higher and more continuous than the Eastern Ghats.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Statement 1 is also correct: Lakshadweep is made of coral atolls. | Trap (C): Statement 3 is also correct. | Trap (D): Statement 2 is also correct.

questions.question_text: Which body regulates the securities (stock) market in India?

options.A: SEBI
options.B: PFRDA
options.C: IRDAI
options.D: NABARD

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Securities and Exchange Board of India, a statutory body since 1992, regulates the securities market.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): PFRDA regulates pension funds. | Trap (C): IRDAI regulates insurance. | Trap (D): NABARD finances agriculture and rural development.

questions.question_text: NABARD, set up in 1982, is the apex institution for financing:

options.A: housing for urban families
options.B: exports and imports
options.C: small industries only
options.D: agriculture and rural development

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development provides refinance and development support for agriculture and rural areas.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): That is the National Housing Bank's role. | Trap (B): That is the role of EXIM Bank. | Trap (C): SIDBI is the apex body for small industries.

questions.question_text: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the share of a bank's deposits that it must:

options.A: pay to depositors as interest
options.B: invest in gold and government securities itself
options.C: keep with the RBI as cash
options.D: lend to priority sectors such as agriculture

questions.pedagogical_explanation: CRR is the portion of net demand and time liabilities that banks must keep as cash balances with the RBI.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): CRR has nothing to do with interest paid. | Trap (B): That describes the Statutory Liquidity Ratio, held by the bank itself. | Trap (D): That is the priority sector lending target.

questions.question_text: 'Stagflation' describes an economy that experiences:

options.A: a fall in prices caused by a sharp rise in unemployment
options.B: falling prices together with rapid economic growth
options.C: high inflation together with stagnant growth and high unemployment
options.D: high growth with moderate and stable inflation

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Stagflation combines stagnation (slow growth, high unemployment) with inflation, as in many economies in the 1970s.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): That is deflation linked to recession. | Trap (B): Falling prices are deflation, the opposite. | Trap (D): That is a healthy boom, not stagflation.

questions.question_text: In India, the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is compiled and released by:

options.B: the Reserve Bank of India

questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The NSO compiles the CPI, not the WPI. | Trap (B): The RBI uses price data but does not compile the WPI. | Trap (D): The Labour Bureau compiles CPI for industrial workers.
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: WPI compiler's long official name makes it the longest option.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI:

questions.question_text: 0 kelvin, the lowest possible temperature, is equal to about:

questions.question_text: A:B = 3:4 and B:C = 6:7. If A + B + C = 350, what is C?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Treats A:B:C as 3:4:7 without first making B the same in both ratios. | Trap (C): This is B's share (12/35 of 350). | Trap (D): This is A's share (9/35 of 350).
questions.concept_tag: Ratio - combining two ratios through a common term

questions.question_text: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹93. What is the sum?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: CI for 3 years = P(1.331 − 1) = 0.331P. SI = 0.30P. Difference = 0.031P = 93, so P = ₹3,000.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Divides 93 by 0.03, treating the difference as 3% of the sum. | Trap (C): Uses the two-year shortcut (difference = P × r²) for a three-year period. | Trap (D): Divides 93 by 0.1, as if the difference were one year's interest.
questions.concept_tag: Compound Interest - CI minus SI over three years

questions.question_text: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many days in all is the job completed?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Take the job as 36 units: A does 3 a day, B does 2. In 4 days together they do 20 units. B does the remaining 16 in 8 days. Total = 4 + 8 = 12 days.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Subtracts the 4 days twice when counting the total. | Trap (C): Gives only the days B works alone after A leaves. | Trap (D): Finds the time if both worked together throughout.
questions.concept_tag: Time & Work - one worker leaves midway

questions.question_text: A 240 m long train crosses a 360 m long platform in 30 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

options.B: 20 km/h
options.D: 72 km/h

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Distance = 240 + 360 = 600 m, covered in 30 s, so speed = 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Uses only the platform's length (360 m). | Trap (B): Finds 20 m/s but does not convert it to km/h. | Trap (C): Uses only the train's length (240 m), ignoring the platform.
questions.concept_tag: Time, Speed & Distance - train crossing a platform

questions.question_text: The average of 11 numbers is 60. The average of the first six is 58 and that of the last six is 63. What is the sixth number?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The sixth number is counted in both groups: 6 × 58 + 6 × 63 − 11 × 60 = 348 + 378 − 660 = 66.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Averages 58 and 63 and rounds up, without using the totals. | Trap (B): Assumes the middle number equals the overall average. | Trap (C): Takes the average of the last six as the shared number.

questions.question_text: When the number N = 3^45 + 5^45 is divided by 8, the remainder obtained is:
questions.pedagogical_explanation: For odd n, aⁿ + bⁿ is divisible by a + b. Here a + b = 8, so the remainder is 0. (Check: 3^odd ≡ 3 and 5^odd ≡ 5 (mod 8); 3 + 5 = 8.)
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Finds 3^45 ≡ 3 (mod 8) but forgets the 5^45 term. | Trap (B): Finds 5^45 ≡ 5 (mod 8) but forgets the 3^45 term. | Trap (D): Takes both powers as ≡ 1 (mod 8), as for even exponents.
questions.concept_tag: Number System - sum of two odd powers
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if (pow(3,45,8)+pow(5,45,8))%8==0 else 'X'

questions.question_text: How many of the divisors of 360 are even?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5 has (3+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 24 divisors. The odd ones use 2⁰ only: (2+1)(1+1) = 6. Even divisors = 24 − 6 = 18.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): This is the number of odd divisors. | Trap (B): This is the total number of divisors of 360. | Trap (C): Halves the total, assuming exactly half of the divisors are even.
questions.verify_code: answer = 'D' if sum(1 for d in range(1,361) if 360%d==0 and d%2==0)==18 else 'X'

questions.question_text: What is the highest power of 12 that divides 50! exactly?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: 12 = 2² × 3. Powers of 2 in 50!: 25+12+6+3+1 = 47, giving 23 pairs. Powers of 3: 16+5+1 = 22. The limit is min(23, 22) = 22.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Counts the multiples of 3 once, ignoring 9 and 27. | Trap (C): Counts only the multiples of 12 up to 50. | Trap (D): Uses the count of 2s (47 ÷ 2 = 23) but forgets that 3s are scarcer.
questions.concept_tag: Number System - highest power of a composite in a factorial
questions.verify_code: answer = 'A' if (lambda f: min(f(2)//2,f(3)))(lambda p: sum(50//pow(p,k) for k in range(1,7)))==22 else 'X'

questions.question_text: By selling an article for ₹1,140, a trader loses 5%. At what price must he sell it to gain 10%?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Adds 10% to the selling price of ₹1,140 instead of to the cost price. | Trap (C): Takes 5% more than the cost price, mixing up the loss and the gain. | Trap (D): Adds 15% (5 + 10) to ₹1,140.
questions.concept_tag: Profit & Loss - from a loss to a target gain
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: Closest to a repo item (0.78 at generation).

questions.question_text: 60 litres of a mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 2:1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1:2?

options.A: 60 litres
options.B: 30 litres
options.C: 40 litres
options.D: 20 litres

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Milk = 40 L and water = 20 L. For milk:water = 1:2, water must be 80 L, so add 80 − 20 = 60 L.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Adds half of the mixture without checking the new ratio. | Trap (C): Doubles the existing water instead of finding the needed total. | Trap (D): Adds only enough water to make milk and water equal.
questions.concept_tag: Mixtures - reversing a ratio by adding water
questions.verify_code: answer = 'A' if 40*2-20==60 else 'X'

questions.question_text: Vessel X contains milk and water in the ratio 3:1 and vessel Y in the ratio 5:3. In what ratio should X and Y be mixed to get a mixture with milk and water in the ratio 2:1?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Assumes equal parts always work. | Trap (B): Compares the milk parts of the two ratios directly. | Trap (D): Reverses the alligation ratio.
questions.concept_tag: Alligation - mixing two mixtures to a target ratio

questions.question_text: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5:7. Six years ago it was 3:5. What will B's age be 8 years from now?

options.A: 23 years
options.B: 27 years
options.C: 29 years
options.D: 21 years

questions.pedagogical_explanation: (5x − 6)/(7x − 6) = 3/5 gives 25x − 30 = 21x − 18, so x = 3. A = 15 and B = 21 now, so B will be 29 in 8 years.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Adds 8 years to A's present age (15) instead of B's. | Trap (B): Adds 6 years instead of 8. | Trap (D): Gives B's present age.
questions.concept_tag: Ages - ratio now and in the past
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if [x for x in range(1,30) if 5*(5*x-6)==3*(7*x-6)][0]*7+8==29 else 'X'

questions.question_text: A and B start together from the same point on a 600 m circular track and run in the same direction at 6 m/s and 10 m/s. After how many seconds will they first be together at the starting point?

options.A: 300 seconds
options.B: 600 seconds
options.C: 150 seconds
options.D: 37.5 seconds

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Lap times: A = 600/6 = 100 s and B = 600/10 = 60 s. They are together at the start after LCM(100, 60) = 300 s.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Multiplies the lap times without taking their LCM. | Trap (C): This is when they first meet anywhere on the track (600 ÷ 4). | Trap (D): Uses the relative speed for opposite directions (600 ÷ 16).
questions.concept_tag: Time, Speed & Distance - meeting at the start on a circular track
questions.verify_code: answer = 'A' if min(t for t in range(1,1000) if t%100==0 and t%60==0)==300 else 'X'

questions.question_text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 hours and 30 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill?

options.A: 15 hours
options.B: 12 hours
options.C: 10 hours
options.D: 60 hours

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/15 = (3 + 2 − 4)/60 = 1/60 of the tank per hour, so 60 hours.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Takes C's emptying time as the answer. | Trap (B): Ignores the outlet C. | Trap (C): Adds C's rate instead of subtracting it.
questions.concept_tag: Pipes & Cisterns - two filling pipes and one outlet

questions.question_text: A starts a business with ₹40,000. B joins 4 months later with ₹60,000 and C joins 6 months after the start with ₹80,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹1,74,000, what is C's share?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Capital × months: A = 40,000 × 12, B = 60,000 × 8, C = 80,000 × 6, all equal to 4,80,000. So the profit is shared equally: ₹58,000 each.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Divides in the capital ratio 2:3:4, ignoring time. | Trap (C): Weights C's capital by 4 months instead of 6. | Trap (D): Gives C half the profit for bringing the largest capital.
questions.concept_tag: Partnership - partners joining at different times

questions.question_text: How many four-digit even numbers have all four digits different?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Units digit 0: 9 × 8 × 7 = 504. Units digit 2, 4, 6 or 8: 4 × 8 × 8 × 7 = 1,792 (first digit not 0 or the units digit). Total = 2,296.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Halves the 4,536 four-digit numbers with distinct digits, as if exactly half were even. | Trap (B): Forgets the case where the last digit is 0. | Trap (D): Lets the first digit be any of 9 digits even after the units digit is fixed.
questions.concept_tag: Counting - even numbers with distinct digits
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if sum(1 for n in range(1000,10000) if n%2==0 and len(set(str(n)))==4)==2296 else 'X'

questions.question_text: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is a prime number?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Wrongly counts the sum 9 (4 ways) as prime. | Trap (C): Counts 14 outcomes, missing the sum 2 (1, 1). | Trap (D): Guesses that about half the sums are prime; only 15 of 36 are.
questions.concept_tag: Probability - prime sum on two dice
questions.verify_code: answer = 'A' if sum(1 for a in range(1,7) for b in range(1,7) if a+b in (2,3,5,7,11))==15 else 'X'

questions.question_text: The area of a circle is 154 cm². What is the area of the largest square that can be drawn inside it? (Take π = 22/7.)

options.A: 49 cm²
options.B: 196 cm²
options.C: 98 cm²
options.D: 154 cm²

questions.pedagogical_explanation: πr² = 154 gives r = 7, so the diameter is 14 cm. The largest square has the diameter as its diagonal: area = 14²/2 = 98 cm².
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Takes the square's side as the radius (7 cm). | Trap (B): Takes the square's side as the diameter (14 cm). | Trap (D): Assumes the square has the same area as the circle.
questions.concept_tag: Mensuration - largest square inside a circle

questions.question_text: What is the sum of all two-digit numbers that leave a remainder of 3 when divided by 7?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Counts 14 terms instead of 13. | Trap (C): Misses the first such number, 10. | Trap (D): Wrongly includes 3, which is not a two-digit number.
questions.concept_tag: Arithmetic Progression - sum of numbers with a given remainder
questions.verify_code: answer = 'B' if sum(n for n in range(10,100) if n%7==3)==676 else 'X'

questions.question_text: In a class of 120 students, 70 like tea, 60 like coffee and 25 like neither. How many like only tea?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): This is everyone who likes tea, including those who also like coffee. | Trap (B): Ignores the 25 who like neither, so takes 'both' as 10. | Trap (C): This is the number who like only coffee.
questions.concept_tag: Sets - only one of two preferences

questions.question_text:
Statements: All pens are books. Some books are bags.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are bags. II. Some bags are books.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.A: Both conclusions follow
options.B: Only conclusion II follows
options.C: Only conclusion I follows
options.D: Neither conclusion follows

questions.pedagogical_explanation: 'Some books are bags' converts to 'Some bags are books', so II follows. The pens need not overlap with the bags, so I does not follow.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Accepts I, which is only a possibility. | Trap (C): The pens may lie in a part of 'books' that has no bags. | Trap (D): Misses II, the direct converse of 'Some books are bags'.

questions.question_text: Introducing a woman, Kunal says, "She is the wife of the only son of my father's father." How is the woman related to Kunal?

options.A: Mother
options.B: Sister
options.C: Grandmother
options.D: Aunt

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The only son of Kunal's paternal grandfather must be Kunal's father. His wife is Kunal's mother.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Reads 'wife of the only son' as a sibling. | Trap (C): Stops one generation too early, at the grandfather's wife. | Trap (D): Treats the only son as an uncle; but Kunal's father is himself his father's father's son.
questions.concept_tag: Blood Relations - only son of the paternal grandfather

questions.question_text: Arun walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 6 m, turns right again and walks 18 m, then turns left and walks 9 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?

options.A: 43 m, south-east
options.B: 17 m, north-east
options.C: 17 m, south-east
options.D: 23 m, south-east

questions.pedagogical_explanation: He ends 6 + 9 = 15 m east and 18 − 10 = 8 m south of the start. Distance = √(15² + 8²) = 17 m, to the south-east.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Adds all the distances walked. | Trap (B): Gets the distance right but does not notice he ends south of the start. | Trap (D): Adds the east and south displacements (15 + 8) instead of using Pythagoras.
questions.concept_tag: Directions - distance and direction after four turns
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if 15*15+8*8==17*17 else 'X'

questions.question_text:
Statement: P > Q ≥ R = S < T
Conclusions: I. P > S II. T > Q
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.A: Only conclusion II follows
options.B: Both conclusions follow
options.C: Neither conclusion follows
options.D: Only conclusion I follows

questions.pedagogical_explanation: P > Q ≥ R = S gives P > S, so I follows. T > S and Q ≥ S tell us nothing about T versus Q, so II does not follow.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): T and Q are both linked to S/R in opposite directions, so they cannot be compared. | Trap (B): Accepts II, which cannot be decided. | Trap (C): Misses I: P > Q ≥ R = S gives P > S.

questions.question_text:
Statement: The city corporation has announced free bus rides for women to increase their use of public transport.
Assumptions: I. The cost of fares is one reason some women avoid buses. II. Men will stop using buses once women ride free.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?

options.A: Neither assumption is implicit
options.B: Both assumptions are implicit
options.C: Only assumption I is implicit
options.D: Only assumption II is implicit

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The policy works only if fares are a barrier for some women, so I is implicit. II plays no part in the decision.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Misses I: removing fares can raise use only if fares put some women off. | Trap (B): Accepts II, which is irrelevant to the goal. | Trap (D): Nothing in the policy depends on men's behaviour.
questions.concept_tag: Statement and Assumption - reason for a policy

questions.question_text: Among five friends, A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is shorter than B. E is taller than C. Who is the third tallest?

options.A: A
options.B: E
options.C: B
options.D: C

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Order from tallest: E > C > A > B > D. A is third.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): E is the tallest. | Trap (C): B is fourth, above only D. | Trap (D): C is second tallest, after E.
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: Borderline CAT-Level statement-assumption item.

questions.question_text: In a certain code, COLD is written as DQOH. How will WARM be written in that code?

options.A: XCTQ
options.B: XCUQ
options.C: YCUQ
options.D: XBSN

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The shifts are +1, +2, +3, +4: C→D, O→Q, L→O, D→H. So W→X, A→C, R→U, M→Q: XCUQ.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Shifts the third letter by +2 instead of +3. | Trap (C): Shifts the first letter by +2 instead of +1. | Trap (D): Shifts every letter by +1.
questions.verify_code: answer = 'B' if ''.join(chr(ord(c)+i+1) for i,c in enumerate('COLD'))=='DQOH' and ''.join(chr(ord(c)+i+1) for i,c in enumerate('WARM'))=='XCUQ' else 'X'

questions.question_text: Five persons B, C, D, A and E sit in a row facing north. B sits at the extreme left. D sits second to the right of B. E is not a neighbour of D. A sits somewhere to the right of C. Who sits between D and E?

options.A: B
options.B: A
options.C: No one
options.D: C

questions.pedagogical_explanation: B = 1 and D = 3. E cannot be 2 or 4, so E = 5. C and A take 2 and 4, with A right of C, so C = 2 and A = 4. Order: B C D A E. A sits between D and E.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): B is at the extreme left, far from E. | Trap (C): E is at the extreme right with A next to it, so A is between D and E. | Trap (D): C sits between B and D.
questions.concept_tag: Arrangement - five persons in a row
questions.verify_code: answer = 'B' if [(c,a,e) for c in (2,4,5) for a in (2,4,5) for e in (2,4,5) if len({c,a,e})==3 and abs(e-3)!=1 and a>c]==[(2,4,5)] else 'X'

questions.question_text: In a class of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the top and Sita is 25th from the bottom. Mohan stands exactly midway between them. What is Mohan's rank from the bottom?

options.A: 27th
options.B: 14th
options.C: 26th
options.D: 28th

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Sita is 40 − 25 + 1 = 16th from the top. The midpoint of 12th and 16th is 14th from the top, which is 40 − 14 + 1 = 27th from the bottom.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): This is Mohan's rank from the top. | Trap (C): Converts from top to bottom without adding 1. | Trap (D): Adds 1 twice when converting from top to bottom.

questions.question_text:
Statements: No cats are dogs. All dogs are pets.
Conclusions: I. Some pets are not cats. II. All pets being cats is a possibility.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.A: Only conclusion II follows
options.B: Only conclusion I follows
options.C: Both conclusions follow
options.D: Neither conclusion follows

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Every dog is a pet and no dog is a cat, so some pets (the dogs) are not cats: I follows. That also rules out all pets being cats, so II does not follow.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): II is impossible: the dogs are pets that are not cats. | Trap (C): Accepts II, which contradicts the statements. | Trap (D): Misses I: the pets that are dogs are not cats.

questions.question_text:
Statements: Some A are B. All B are C. No C is D.
Conclusions: I. Some A are not D. II. Some C are A. III. No B is D.
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.A: Only II and III follow
options.B: Only III follows
options.C: All three conclusions follow
options.D: Only I and II follow

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Some A are B and all B are C, so some A are C, hence II. All B are C and no C is D, so no B is D, hence III. The A that are B are not D, so some A are not D, hence I.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Misses I: the A that are B are C, so they are not D. | Trap (B): Misses both chains through 'Some A are B'. | Trap (D): Misses III: all B are C, and no C is D.
questions.concept_tag: Syllogism - three statements and three conclusions

questions.question_text: P + Q means P is the father of Q; P − Q means P is the mother of Q; P × Q means P is the brother of Q; P ÷ Q means P is the sister of Q. If A + B × C − D, how is A related to D?

options.A: Maternal grandfather
options.B: Uncle
options.C: Father
options.D: Paternal grandfather

questions.pedagogical_explanation: A is B's father. B is C's brother, so A is also C's father. C is D's mother. So A is D's mother's father: maternal grandfather.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): That is B's relation to D. | Trap (C): A is the father of B and C, a generation above D's parent. | Trap (D): C is D's mother, so A is on the mother's side.
questions.concept_tag: Coded Blood Relations - symbols for relationships

questions.question_text: M is the sister of N. N is the son of O. O is the wife of P. Q is the father of P. How is M related to Q?

options.A: Granddaughter
options.B: Grandson
options.C: Niece
options.D: Daughter

questions.pedagogical_explanation: N is O's son and M is N's sister, so M is also O's child. O is P's wife, so M is P's daughter. Q is P's father, so M is Q's granddaughter.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): M is a sister, so female. | Trap (C): Treats P as M's uncle rather than her father. | Trap (D): M is P's daughter, not Q's.
questions.concept_tag: Blood Relations - grandchild through a parent's spouse

questions.question_text: Each of A, B and C either always tells the truth or always lies. A says, "B is a liar." B says, "C is a liar." C says, "A and B are both liars." Who tells the truth?

options.A: Only A
options.B: Only B
options.C: A and C
options.D: Only C

questions.pedagogical_explanation: If A is truthful, B lies, so C tells the truth, but C says A lies: impossible. So A lies, meaning B is truthful. Then C is a liar, and C's claim is indeed false since B is truthful. Only B tells the truth.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): If A is truthful, B lies, so C is truthful, but C then says A lies: a contradiction. | Trap (C): C calls A a liar, so they cannot both be truthful. | Trap (D): If C is truthful, A and B both lie, but A's lie would make B truthful: a contradiction.
questions.verify_code: answer = 'B' if [(a,b,c) for a in (0,1) for b in (0,1) for c in (0,1) if a==(b==0) and b==(c==0) and c==(a==0 and b==0)]==[(0,1,0)] else 'X'

questions.question_text:
On what day of the week did 1 March fall in a particular year?
Statement I: 1 February of that year was a Monday.
Statement II: That year was a leap year.

options.A: Statement II alone is sufficient
options.B: Even both together are not sufficient
options.C: Statement I alone is sufficient
options.D: Both statements together are needed, and they are sufficient

questions.pedagogical_explanation: From I, 1 March is 28 or 29 days after a Monday. II makes it 29 days, so 1 March is a Tuesday. Both are needed.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): II gives no starting weekday. | Trap (B): Together they fix February at 29 days, so 1 March is a Tuesday. | Trap (C): Without knowing whether February has 28 or 29 days, 1 March could be Monday or Tuesday.
questions.concept_tag: Data Sufficiency - day of the week
questions.verify_code: answer = 'D' if 29%7==1 else 'X'

questions.question_text:
Statement I: Prices of vegetables in the city have risen sharply this month.
Statement II: Heavy rains damaged crops in the nearby districts last month.
Which of the following holds?

options.A: The two statements are independent
options.B: Both statements are effects of a common cause
options.C: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
options.D: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Last month's crop damage cut supply to the city, which raised prices this month. II is the cause and I the effect.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Lower supply from nearby districts directly pushes up city prices. | Trap (B): Crop damage directly explains the price rise; no separate cause is needed. | Trap (C): Reverses the time order: the crop damage came first.
questions.concept_tag: Cause and Effect - two related statements

questions.question_text:
Statements: A ≥ B > C; D < C ≤ E; F > E
Conclusions: I. A > D II. F > C III. B ≥ E
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.A: Only I and III follow
options.B: All three follow
options.C: Only II follows
options.D: Only I and II follow

questions.pedagogical_explanation: A ≥ B > C > D gives A > D (I). F > E ≥ C gives F > C (II). B > C and E ≥ C do not fix B against E, so III does not follow.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): B and E are both above C, but they cannot be compared. | Trap (B): Accepts III, which cannot be decided. | Trap (C): Misses I: A ≥ B > C > D gives A > D.

questions.question_text: Four lectures P, Q, R and S are held one each on Monday to Thursday. R is on the day immediately after P. S is on some day before Q. Q is on neither Monday nor Thursday. S is not on Wednesday. Which lecture is on Wednesday?

options.A: R
options.B: P
options.C: Q
options.D: S

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Q is on Tuesday or Wednesday. If Q is Wednesday, S is Monday or Tuesday and P–R needs two consecutive free days, which is impossible. So Q is Tuesday, S is Monday (before Q), and P–R are Wednesday–Thursday.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): R comes the day after P, which is Thursday. | Trap (C): Q is on Tuesday. | Trap (D): S cannot be on Wednesday.
questions.concept_tag: Scheduling - four lectures on four days
questions.verify_code: answer = 'B' if [(p,q,r,s) for p in range(4) for q in range(4) for r in range(4) for s in range(4) if len({p,q,r,s})==4 and r==p+1 and s<q and q not in (0,3) and s!=2]==[(2,1,3,0)] else 'X'

questions.question_text: Of 100 students, 50 play cricket, 40 football and 30 hockey. 15 play both cricket and football, 10 football and hockey, and 12 cricket and hockey. 5 play all three. How many play exactly one game?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Only cricket = 50 − 15 − 12 + 5 = 28. Only football = 40 − 15 − 10 + 5 = 20. Only hockey = 30 − 10 − 12 + 5 = 13. Exactly one = 28 + 20 + 13 = 61.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): This is the number who play at least one game. | Trap (B): This is the number who play exactly two games. | Trap (D): This is the number who play none.
questions.concept_tag: Venn Reasoning - exactly one of three games

questions.question_text: Every club member who plays chess also plays carrom. No one who plays carrom is under 15. Riya, a club member, is 13. Which of the following must be true?

options.A: All carrom players in the club play chess
options.B: No club member is under 15
options.C: Riya plays carrom but not chess
options.D: Riya does not play chess

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Riya is under 15, so she does not play carrom. Every chess player plays carrom, so she cannot play chess.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The statements say only that chess players play carrom, not the reverse. | Trap (B): Riya herself is a 13-year-old member. | Trap (C): Riya is under 15, so she cannot play carrom.

questions.question_text: 15 August 1947 was a Friday. What day of the week was 15 August 1950?

options.A: Wednesday
options.B: Monday
options.C: Tuesday
options.D: Sunday

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Odd days: 15 Aug 1947 → 1948 includes 29 Feb 1948, so 2; then 1 and 1. Total 4. Friday + 4 = Tuesday.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Counts two leap years in the period. | Trap (B): Forgets the extra day from 29 February 1948. | Trap (D): Adds only two odd days.
questions.concept_tag: Calendar - weekday a few years later across a leap day
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if (366+365+365)%7==4 and ['Fri','Sat','Sun','Mon','Tue','Wed','Thu'][4]=='Tue' else 'X'

questions.question_text: A wall clock shows twenty minutes past seven. Find the smaller angle formed between its two hands.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Gives the reflex angle instead of the smaller one. | Trap (C): Moves the hour hand back instead of forward. | Trap (D): Counts the three 30° gaps from 4 to 7 and forgets that the hour hand has moved 10° past 7.
questions.verify_code: answer = 'B' if abs(30*7*2-11*20)==200 else 'X'

questions.question_text: Find the next term: 1, 4, 27, 256, ?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The terms are 1¹, 2², 3³, 4⁴, so the next is 5⁵ = 3125.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): An arithmetic slip near 5⁵. | Trap (B): Takes 5⁴ instead of 5⁵. | Trap (C): Takes 4⁵, mixing up base and exponent.
questions.concept_tag: Number Series - n to the power n
questions.verify_code: answer = 'D' if [pow(n,n) for n in range(1,6)]==[1,4,27,256,3125] else 'X'

questions.question_text: In a certain code, TEACHER is written as VGCEJGT. How is STUDENT written in that code?

options.A: UVWFGPV
options.B: QRSBCLR
options.C: TUVEFOU
options.D: UVWFGOV

questions.pedagogical_explanation: Each letter moves forward by 2: S→U, T→V, U→W, D→F, E→G, N→P, T→V.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Shifts every letter backwards by 2. | Trap (C): Shifts every letter by +1 instead of +2. | Trap (D): Shifts N by +1 instead of +2.
questions.verify_code: answer = 'A' if ''.join(chr(ord(c)+2) for c in 'TEACHER')=='VGCEJGT' and ''.join(chr(ord(c)+2) for c in 'STUDENT')=='UVWFGPV' else 'X'

questions.question_text: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the hands of a clock be together?

options.A: 22 2/11 minutes past 4
options.B: 20 minutes past 4
options.C: 21 9/11 minutes past 4
options.D: 21 3/11 minutes past 4

questions.pedagogical_explanation: The minute hand gains 5.5° a minute and starts 120° behind, so it takes 120/5.5 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Uses 5.5 minutes per 30° instead of the correct rate. | Trap (B): Forgets that the hour hand keeps moving after 4:00. | Trap (D): Gets the fraction wrong when dividing 240 by 11.
questions.concept_tag: Clocks - hands coinciding between two hours
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if 240//11==21 and 240%11==9 else 'X'

questions.question_text: A die has the numbers 1 to 6 on its faces. In one position, 1 is on top, 2 faces you and 3 is on the right. The die is then turned a quarter-turn about its vertical axis, so that 1 stays on top, 3 now faces you and 5 is on the right. Which number is opposite 2?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The quarter-turn brings the old right face (3) to the front and the old back face to the right. So 5 was the back face in the first position, directly opposite 2 at the front.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Assumes the numbers run in order around the die. | Trap (B): 3 is next to 2 (seen together in the first position), so it cannot be opposite. | Trap (D): Picks the one face not seen in either view; the second view shows 5 behind 2.
questions.concept_tag: Dice - opposite face from two positions
questions.review_note: Faculty flag: Dice described in words; check the quarter-turn wording reads clearly.

questions.question_text: How many squares of all sizes are there in a 4 × 4 grid of unit squares?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Misses the single 4 × 4 square, the whole grid. | Trap (C): Counts only the 1 × 1 squares. | Trap (D): Counts only the 1 × 1 and 2 × 2 squares.
questions.concept_tag: Counting Figures - squares in a 4 by 4 grid
questions.verify_code: answer = 'A' if sum(k*k for k in range(1,5))==30 else 'X'

questions.question_text: Among the integers 1 to 300, how many are multiples of 4 that are not multiples of 6?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Multiples of 4: 75. Those also divisible by 6 are multiples of 12: 25. Answer: 75 − 25 = 50.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Counts numbers divisible by 4 or 6 (75 + 50 − 25). | Trap (B): Counts all multiples of 4. | Trap (D): Counts the multiples of 12, the ones to be removed.
questions.concept_tag: Counting - divisible by one number but not another
questions.verify_code: answer = 'C' if sum(1 for n in range(1,301) if n%4==0 and n%6!=0)==50 else 'X'

questions.question_text: In a code language, A stands for addition, B for subtraction, C for multiplication and D for division. Evaluate: 24 D 4 C 3 A 7 B 5
questions.pedagogical_explanation: 24 ÷ 4 × 3 + 7 − 5. Division and multiplication go left to right: 6 × 3 = 18. Then 18 + 7 − 5 = 20.
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Does the multiplication 4 × 3 before the division, so 24 ÷ 12 + 7 − 5. | Trap (B): Swaps the last two signs: 18 − 7 + 5. | Trap (C): Adds 5 instead of subtracting it.
questions.verify_code: answer = 'D' if 24//4*3+7-5==20 else 'X'

questions.question_text:
Find the missing number. In each group, the two numbers produce the third by the same rule.
(5, 4) → 11
(6, 3) → 9
(7, 5) → ?
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Rule: product − sum. 20 − 9 = 11 and 18 − 9 = 9, so 35 − 12 = 23.
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Uses product − sum + 1, which does not fit (5, 4) → 11. | Trap (C): Uses only the product. | Trap (D): Uses only the sum.
